newsitem.title: ITALY: FORECAST-Italy May PSBR seen at 10.5 trln lire.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Italy May PSBR seen at 10.5 trln lire.

text.p: Italy's public sector borrowing requirement (PSBR) is likely to reach 10.5 trillion lire in May, up on the 7.5 trillion lire needed in May 1996, analysts polled by Reuters said.
But the cumulative PSBR for the first six months of this year is likely to be lower than the same period in 1996 with analysts forecasting 24 trillion for January to June.
This would be one trillion less than the 25 trillion expected by the Italian Treasury and less than half of the 53.75 trillion needed in the first half of 1996.
For May, the year on year comparison for the budget deficit includes excess funds paid back in May last year into Treasury coffers from state bodies and public authorities.

"In May 1996 pensions payments were also postponed to the start of the following month. The postponement lightened the monthly borrowing requirement by 2.5 trillion lire," said Moreno Capretti at Banca Commerciale Italiana.
The outlook for June's PSBR is for a surplus of 28 trillion, with encouraging trends in corporate income tax after reasonable 1996 corporate and banking results.

In addition, June revenue from this year's exceptional levy, the so-called Euro tax, will be boosted by a first tranche payment by the self-employed, who pay the tax in two lumps, and the regular monthly revenue from the tax levied at source on company employees.
Analysts noted, however, that the first half of the year is not the most difficult for public accounts.
Giuliano Gasparini at research group Prometeia said: "The most difficult months are from September to November, those are the months when it's difficult to contain spending."
For now, analysts say the Treasury is keeping control of spending by ministries and local authorities.
"They are accumulating surpluses which could allow the Treasury to make further savings in coming months," said Ilaria Fornari at JP Morgan.

But JP Morgan said for Italy to reach the three percent budget deficit to gross domestic product ratio needed by the year end to join a single European currency in 1999, the Treasury must save 40 trillion lire in the second half of the year in respect to levels seen in the last three years.

The last official figures for Italy's public accounts were Treasury data in early May which put PSBR in the first four months of 1997 at 42 trillion lire compared with 71.67 trillion in the same 1996 period.

** The forecast figure is the difference between a 74.30 trillion lire PA net deficit forecast in the March 1997 report on state accounts and the 15.5 trillion lire of deficit-cutting measures contained in this year's mini-budget.
